payload.prompt: What is Microsoft Foundry?

options.text: A platform for building and managing AI apps and agents
options.rationale: Microsoft Foundry is a unified Azure platform for AI applications and agents. It brings together lifecycle capabilities such as models, governance, and monitoring.

options.text: An Azure resource that provides platform capabilities
options.rationale: A Foundry resource is a narrower Azure component. It is not the overall Microsoft Foundry platform.
options.better_fit: Use this description when defining a Foundry resource.

feedback.intrinsic: This identifies a narrower component.
feedback.instructional: Microsoft Foundry is the broader platform.

options.text: A workspace inside a Foundry resource
options.rationale: A Foundry project is a workspace within a resource. It does not describe the complete platform.
options.better_fit: Use this description when defining a Foundry project.

feedback.intrinsic: This selects the wrong organizational level.
feedback.instructional: A project is a workspace; Foundry is the platform.

options.text: A service used only to store datasets
options.rationale: Foundry supports far more than dataset storage. It supports building, deploying, governing, and managing AI solutions.
options.better_fit: This would fit a data-storage-only service.

feedback.intrinsic: This omits core capabilities.
feedback.instructional: Foundry supports the AI application lifecycle.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Foundry is the unified Azure platform for AI applications and agents.

payload.prompt: Is the following statement accurate?
payload.statement: Microsoft Foundry is only a workspace inside a Foundry resource.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. A project is the workspace; Foundry is the broader platform.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This assigns Foundry the wrong scope.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Foundry is a platform, while a project is a workspace.

payload.prompt: Which actions can developers perform with the Foundry model catalog? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The catalog lets developers browse available models. It includes first-party, partner, and open-source choices.
Playgrounds and leaderboards support model evaluation. Teams can compare candidates before deployment.
Foundry supports managing and deploying selected models. Deployment makes a model available to an application.
Speech-to-text is an Azure Speech capability. The catalog supports the model-selection lifecycle.
options.better_fit: Choose this when selecting Azure Speech for spoken input.

feedback.intrinsic: This does not perform catalog work.
feedback.instructional: Use Azure Speech for speech conversion.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The catalog supports browsing, evaluation, and deployment.

payload.prompt: Evaluate this statement.
payload.statement: Foundry supports models from first-party, partner, and open-source sources.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The catalog includes all three source categories.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Foundry includes first-party, partner, and open-source models.

payload.prompt: True or false?
payload.statement: Foundry model deployments can use only the batch deployment type.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Standard and provisioned deployments are also supported.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This rules out valid deployment options.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Foundry supports standard, provisioned, and batch deployments.

payload.prompt: Arrange the model-release process in order.
payload.explanation: Teams first discover options, then evaluate and select one before deployment.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The process would deploy before making a selection.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Browse first, evaluate next, then select and deploy.

payload.prompt: A support team must choose and release a chat model for a new application. Which catalog actions should it take? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Browsing reveals suitable model options. This starts the selection process.

options.text: Compare models in leaderboards or playgrounds
options.rationale: Evaluation tools let the team compare candidates. This informs a deployment decision.
The selected model must be deployed for application use. Foundry supports that release step.

options.text: Create a knowledge base before selecting a model
options.rationale: A knowledge base grounds answers with data. It does not substitute for model selection and deployment.
options.better_fit: Choose this when the app needs connected organizational knowledge.

feedback.intrinsic: The model decision remains unresolved.
feedback.instructional: Use the catalog to browse, evaluate, and deploy models.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Browse, evaluate, select, and deploy.

payload.prompt: A product manager must compare models for a regulated application, deploy one under controls, and address safety. Which capabilities fit? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The catalog supports comparing model alternatives. It directly supports the selection decision.
Governance supports controlled deployment. That addresses the regulated-release requirement.
Safety support addresses the stated risk requirement. It is relevant to a regulated AI release.
Azure Speech converts between speech and text. It does not evaluate models or govern deployment.
options.better_fit: Choose this when the application needs voice input or output.

feedback.intrinsic: The governance and safety needs remain unmet.
feedback.instructional: Use catalog, governance, and safety capabilities here.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. These capabilities support comparison, controlled deployment, and safety.

payload.prompt: What can an AI agent do?

options.text: Reason, call tools, use data, and automate workflows
options.rationale: An AI agent is task-oriented and reasons over input. It can use data, call tools, and automate work.
Speech conversion is performed by Azure Speech. Agents coordinate broader task workflows.
options.better_fit: Use this description for Azure Speech.

feedback.intrinsic: This omits agent behavior.
feedback.instructional: Agents can call tools and automate workflows.

options.rationale: Foundry IQ provides knowledge grounding. An agent can use that knowledge while also reasoning and acting.
options.better_fit: Use this description for a knowledge retrieval layer.

feedback.intrinsic: This reduces an agent to retrieval.
feedback.instructional: Agents can use knowledge as part of a workflow.

options.rationale: Model hosting makes a model available. An agent is the system that coordinates task execution.
options.better_fit: Use this description for model-hosting capability.

feedback.intrinsic: This omits the workflow.
feedback.instructional: Hosting and agent behavior are distinct.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Agents reason, use data, call tools, and automate work.

Azure Language supports language tasks such as summarization and classification. It is a Foundry Tool.
Azure Speech supports speech-to-text and text-to-speech. It is a Foundry Tool.
Foundry IQ is a permission-aware knowledge layer. It is not an individual vision, language, or speech service.

Azure Speech transcribes spoken questions. It meets the speech-to-text need.
Azure Language extracts key phrases from text. It can process the transcript.
Foundry IQ grounds answers using connected data. It does not analyze product images.
options.better_fit: Choose this for permission-aware answers from organization data.

feedback.intrinsic: The photos remain unanalyzed.

payload.prompt: A clinical-assistance app must inspect a medical image, summarize accompanying text, and read the summary aloud. Which Foundry Tools fit? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Azure Vision analyzes images. It addresses the medical-image requirement.

Azure Speech can synthesize spoken output. It addresses the read-aloud requirement.
